1) NAD+ plays a critical role in the regulation of aging and age-related disorders, including neurodegeneration; 2) NAD+ is required to regulate mitochondrial function and sirtuin activity; 3) NAD+ supplementation may represent a new treatment for neurodegenerative disorders, and 4) the NAD+ precursory molecule nicotinamide riboside may represent a novel, safe, and efficacious treatment for neurodegeneration.
NAD+ levels decrease with age in many tissues and that increasing NAD+ levels can improve health and lifespan.

NAD+ is a key regulator of metabolism, aging, and neurodegenerative disorders and that supplementation of the NAD+ precursor nicotinamide riboside (NR) can be an effective therapy for these conditions.

the study of the mechanisms that regulate the aging process and the development of new therapeutic strategies for the prevention and treatment of neurodegenerative and age-associated diseases.

understanding the role that the sirtuin enzymes play in aging and age-related diseases, and with developing small-molecule sirtuin modulators as potential therapies.
